summary:
The Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2024 provides funding and establishes spending guidelines for the Department of Defense and related intelligence programs for fiscal year 2024. 

The Act includes several general provisions governing the use of appropriated funds. It prohibits modifications to the National Intelligence Program (NIP) appropriations account structure and budget presentation, with exceptions for mergers at or below the Expenditure Center level. The Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense may jointly study alternative financial management processes for auditability, provided they include a counterintelligence risk assessment. Funds for intelligence activities are deemed specifically authorized until the enactment of the FY2024 Intelligence Authorization Act. Office of the Director of National Intelligence funds expire at the end of the current fiscal year, except for research and technology funds, which are available until September 30, 2025, and real property purchases, available until September 30, 2026. Additionally, funds cannot be used to integrate foreign intelligence information unless it was lawfully collected during authorized activities, with U.S. person information handled per the Fourth Amendment and Executive Order 12333.

For military construction and family support, the Act permits up to $11,000,000 each from Operation and Maintenance (O&M) accounts for the Army, Navy, and Air Force to be transferred to a central Fisher House fund. It also appropriates $5,000,000 for a grant to the Fisher House Foundation for constructing and furnishing additional Fisher Houses. Up to $1,000,000 may be transferred from O&M Navy to the John C. Stennis Center Trust Fund.

Regarding international cooperative programs, the Act allocates $500,000,000 from Procurement Defense-Wide and RDT&E Defense-Wide for Israeli cooperative programs. This includes $80,000,000 for Iron Dome procurement, $127,000,000 for the SRBMD program, $40,000,000 for SRBMD co-production, $80,000,000 for Arrow 3 Upper Tier co-production, and $173,000,000 for the Arrow System Improvement Program.

For shipbuilding, $1,648,559,000 is provided from the Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy (SCN) account, available until September 30, 2024, to cover prior-year shipbuilding cost increases across 17 line items. The largest allocations are $624,600,000 for Carrier Replacement and $355,166,000 for T-AGOS Surtass. SCN subdivisions are deemed the same purpose as prior-year subdivisions, with a 1% limitation applying to the total appropriation.

The Act imposes several prohibitions and restrictions. It bars funds for the research, procurement, or deployment of nuclear-armed missile defense interceptors. It prohibits the decommissioning of any Littoral Combat Ship, the USS Germantown, or the USS Tortuga. It prohibits reducing or disestablishing the 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron below funded levels. It also prohibits transferring Tactical Unmanned Aerial Vehicle research, development, and acquisition authority from the Army. 

Furthermore, the Act prohibits reprogramming funds to create new programs unless immediately necessary for national security and following prior written notification to congressional defense committees. It prohibits modifying Navy command and control relationships to give Fleet Forces Command operational or administrative control of Pacific Fleet Navy forces, maintaining the status quo from October 1, 2004, unless a written modification is proposed to Congress. Finally, notices required under 10 U.S.C. §3601 must be submitted concurrently to the House and Senate Defense Appropriations Subcommittees.
